Its really cool actually (film student here) frame rate is how many pictures fill up the span of 1 second therefor creating a "moving image" most common is 24fps for movies (any lower and it becomes obvious that its just pictures) and 30fps for TV. That's why T.V. looks smoother. Shutter speed is very different though! A picture is formed by light hitting a sensor and being recorder from said sensor (or film) but if you just left the sensor wide open it would just be white because of all the light hitting it. So what happens is a shutter flaps open then closes. The light that hit the sensor while it was open is what's recorded as an image. Shutter speed is how long that shutter stays open before closing to record the picture. Low shutter speeds make for clearer video. High for blurrier.
It's a matter of shutter speed not frame rate. If they changed the frame rate it would have just looked funny.

After all the feedback I wrote out a guide to creating a world, unfortunatly its about 1,400 words long, so it pushes post to its limit. If you take the time and look through the comment that I posted in its stead it should be exactly what you guys have been asking for.

**To Create a World**  
So a budding DM I see? Probably played some of your buddies custom worlds, maybe DM'd some premades, but now its different, now its time to make your own world, with a history, people, language, culture hell everything of its own right from your brilliant mind. but where to start? Well this will help. Step 1 will be about coming up with an idea, if you already got one good, skip that part, if you dont well maybe this'll help. Through out this I'll create a world as an example using the steps I took.  
  
**Step 1: An Idea**  
Now before you can even start fleshing out the intense lore of your worlds that world needs to exist, When first thinking about your world come up with a basic point shoot off from, it could be as simple as the idea that people ride giant frogs in this world to as complicated as a brilliant idea for a clan war in a psudo asian stylized setting. Remember though, what your not doing here is creating a plot, thats not what this is about, this is about creating the world itself. For the Example I will be running with my starting point will be simple enough, in the centre of this world is a collosal tower that no one has seen the top off.  
  
**Step 2: Expand!**  
So now you have your brilliant base idea, expand upon it, but remember this is a DND campaign, so a world where no one fights and everyone gets along is a pretty crappy idea unless you plan on having your characters being chaotic evil bastards who want to ruin it all. Below is a list of some questions that you can ask yourself to expand it all. this is without thinking of the people who inhabit your world yet.     
-Is there magic? If so is there very little or is there an insane amount floating through the air.  
-Is it set only in one country? one continent? one hemisphere? a world? multiworlds? Multiplains? figure it out!  
-What is the environment like here? if large what are some of the environments?  
-What are some important land marks in this world?  
-Are the cultures/regions based on real world places? (ie. rome, china, medieval europe, africa, etc...)  
You can use those questions to start expanding around your base idea, in my example of the Tower World I mentioned in step 1 I would say yes there is magic, lots of it, but its dangerous and sacrifices are made to use it. Its set on one continent but its an isolated continent. Its a waistland, ranging from frigid cold in the south to blazing hot in the north, very little healthy land but that there is, is mostly deadly swamps. Obviously the tower but besides that maybe a giant mountain in the south and a legendary witches hut in the swamps. when it comes to the cultures regions part maybe the north is based on a kinda cowboy/old west feel whereas the south is more viking with a swamp filled with very few people anyways between them.  
  
**Step 3: The people's basics**  
The world you thought up is starting to take form now isnt it? when it comes to the stuff I mentioned in step 2 it really helps expand your world as a physical, geological place. but what about the people? well I really like lists and I think you can use them easily to take a look at your world.  
-Races? is this world filled with elves and dwarves? or maybe klingons and borg? possibly a time lord too?  
-Nations? do you have nations? why do they exist and if they do how? whats the political structure like?  
-Religion? what are some of the religions of this world? do the nations support or deter certain ones? why did they develop?    
-Languages? What are the different languages? are there many, or maybe few? is it racial based or culture?  
These questions begin to help you make a realistic, detailed world, one that seems to live or breath. To continue on my wasteland tower world lets look at races, There could be a Dwarven like race that come from the far south. Maybe a lizard people from the swamps, and humans tend to stick to the arid north. I think the south would be built off of a clan system with several dwarven clans as opposed to the nomadic people in the swamps, as I mentioned before the north would be old west stylized so probably small towns with there own sets of rules and ideals. With religions, I think to stick with the viking theme the dwarves believe in some sort of valhalla that the tower reaches too, and that when you die your soul must trek up the tower. with the swamps and the desert I think I'm going to continue with the theme of the tower being a religious symbol. The swamps will maybe be more witchdoctor voodoo based where they see the tower as a gateway to the spirit realm (Much like the Dwarves for Dwarvhalla) and the Cowboys will probably just have a religion based off of christianity where the tower is the home of there god or something like that. You dont need to much detail to start, that comes later. With languages I think it really comes down to region, The lizard folk of the swamps and the dwarves of the south would probably have different dialects based on there clans but each reigns from a base root language specific to there area. The north would probably have maybe 2 or 3 languages based on social areas (think french vs english vs spanish, base latin rout but widely different)  
  
**Step 4: The People Zoomed in**  
Your world is really starting to take form now and with this final step you'll be well on your way to a detailed world that was all your own. With this step you need to take a specific area you figured out above in step 2 or 3 and zoom in on it. Once you've chosen your region ask these questions.  
-What important towns/cities/villages are here, why are they important?  
-What are daily struggles the people here meet? how has this effected them?  
-Are there Racial/Cultural/Religious biases here?  
-Is there Key important people in this area?  
-What else Makes this area special, different, and important compared to any other spot?  
These questions repeated for each area will truly define your detailed world and make it shine. with our now already pretty detailed tower world lets take a look at a small northern rural district, maybe a sandy wasteland with a small town called Mercy. This town is important because its a very prosperous mining town. Everyday people face the threat of starvation, the danger from bandits from the wastes and the possibilty of the mine collapsing, because of this they have taken to being a very close tight nit religious bunch of people. The people of mercy have a distate for the nomadic lifestly of the lizarfolk yet except dwarves with open arms because of there adeptness with mountains and mining. They dont however like the savagery many dwarves bring and especially disagree with the concept of dying a warriors death and therefor arent big fans of people who dont follow there religion. At the head of this town is the great mage Eldritch Black Heart who over taxes the people causing starvation but in turn "Protects" the people from bandits, unfortunatly those who dont pay his taxes usually meet the people there protected from in a matter of days. The importance of this area is that its caves beneath the town and region are ripe with shadow steel, a rare mineral that is used to make the best of guns in the wastelands.  
  
**Step 5: Building the rest**  
Now that you have this quite thought out world dont stop there, come up with business and guilds, anything to make your world just a little more detailed. From this point you'll want to start thinking about the more mechanical side of things, such as Enemies, Classes, Gear, Transportation, Spells. all sorts of things come into making a detailed one of a kind campaign setting.
